context: On your PC and Mac, local sessions load a GitHub plugin that has no token, so its tools fail. claude-settings does not switch it on (checked main 54be9f1), so it is switched on somewhere else on each machine. Every PR step already works through the gh command.

options.gain: Nothing fails, and there is no extra token to keep.
options.how: A local session finds where it is switched on and turns it off; claude-settings records that it stays off.
options.label: Turn the plugin off
options.lose: Nothing that gh does not already do.

options.gain: Sessions get the plugin's GitHub tools as well as gh.
options.how: You create a GitHub token and set it on each machine.
options.label: Give it a token
options.lose: One more token to rotate, on every machine.

ref: c87 (local sessions stop failing on the GitHub plugin's empty token)
title: Local sessions fail on the GitHub plugin's empty token: turn the plugin off, or give it a token?
why: gh covers every PR step, so (b) adds a token for no new outcome.
